summary.text: Plasmodium is a genus of single-celled eukaryotes that are obligate parasites of vertebrates and of insects such as mosquitoes in the genus Anopheles.
A blood-feeding insect injects the parasites into a vertebrate during a blood meal, and they grow in body tissue, often the liver, before infecting red blood cells.
The destruction of host red blood cells can result in malaria, and parasites picked up by another blood-feeding insect continue the life cycle.

facts.label: First identified
facts.value: In the late 19th century by Charles Laveran

facts.label: Deadliest species
facts.value: P. falciparum, killing hundreds of thousands a year

facts.label: Genome
facts.value: Split into 14 chromosomes in the nucleus

items.prompt: A patient with malaria shares a home with her sister. Can the parasite pass between them through everyday contact?

options.label: Yes, through shared air
Yes, by touching infected skin
No, it cannot be spread from person to person
Only through shared food

items.explain: Plasmodium cannot be spread from person to person; it is introduced by an insect bite, and blood transfusion is very rare.

items.prompt: Plasmodium has just been injected by a mosquito bite. Where does it go first?

options.label: Liver or other tissue, replicating once before entering red blood cells
Straight into red blood cells, where it bursts them
The spleen, where it waits for symptoms
The brain, where it multiplies

items.explain: Parasites first infect the liver or other tissue and undergo a single large round of replication before exiting to infect erythrocytes.

items.prompt: Doctors keep developing new drugs against Plasmodium. What has the parasite done in response to each one?

options.label: Died out in the regions where it was used
Evolved resistance to it
Turned harmless to people
Moved to hosts that are not vertebrates

items.explain: A number of drugs have been developed, but the parasites have evolved resistance to each drug developed.

items.prompt: Some primate Plasmodium species can stay hidden in the liver for over a year. What is this dormant stage called?

options.label: Merozoite
Gametocyte
Apicoplast
Hypnozoite

items.explain: Some species of Plasmodium of primates can form a long-lived dormant stage called a hypnozoite, which can remain in the liver for more than a year.

items.prompt: A person infected with Plasmodium has no symptoms at all. Can the parasites still be multiplying inside them?

options.label: Yes, in large numbers hidden in places such as the spleen and bone marrow
No, no symptoms means the parasites have been cleared
Yes, but only inside the liver
Only if a mosquito bites them again

items.explain: Plasmodium infection can be asymptomatic, yet there can be very large numbers of multiplying parasites concealed in the spleen and bone marrow.

items.prompt: A Plasmodium cell is growing inside a red blood cell. Does it need its mitochondrion's ATP-making function there?

options.label: Yes, it is the parasite's only energy source in red cells
Yes, since red blood cells lack energy to share
No, that function is only needed to survive in the insect host
No, because Plasmodium has no mitochondrion

items.explain: The mitochondrion can generate ATP, but this function is only required for survival in the insect host and not for growth in red blood cells.
